about.title: Pittsburg Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: A faulty product does not care where you bought it. In Pittsburg, that might mean a space heater from a Railroad Avenue storefront, a power tool delivered to a home near Harbor Street, or a tire that gave out on SR-4 during the Wednesday morning commute. Pittsburg recorded 170 injury collisions in 2025, with 237 people hurt and 3 lives lost, and when a crash traces back to a part that failed rather than a driver's mistake, product liability law may apply. California treats these claims differently from most injury cases. Under strict liability, you generally do not have to prove the manufacturer was careless. You show the product had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect and that the defect caused your injury. Responsibility can reach the maker, the distributor, and the retailer that sold it. LawProactive is not a law firm. We are a free service that connects Pittsburg residents with an independent attorney who takes product cases on contingency, so there is no fee unless there is a recovery.

whyChoose.title: Why Pittsburg Residents Use LawProactive for Product Cases

items.title: Strict liability changes the question
items.desc: In California you usually do not have to prove the company was negligent, only that the product was defective and the defect caused your injury. The attorneys we connect you with build cases around that standard.

items.title: Every link in the chain can be accountable
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and the Pittsburg or online retailer that sold the item may all share responsibility. An independent attorney can sort out who belongs in the claim.

items.title: Preserving the product comes first
items.desc: The broken item is often the single most important piece of evidence. We move quickly so a lawyer can help you secure it before it is discarded, repaired, or returned.

items.question: My car's airbag did not deploy in a crash on SR-4 in Pittsburg. Is that a product liability case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It may be both, and that is common. The other driver's insurance is one avenue, while a claim against the airbag or vehicle manufacturer is a separate strict liability question about whether the component was defective. Keep the vehicle from being scrapped or repaired until an attorney has had a chance to look at it. We can connect you with someone who handles both sides.

items.question: I threw away the product that hurt me. Do I still have a claim?
items.answer: Losing the product makes things harder, but it does not always end the case. Receipts, photos, packaging, the model number, medical records, and similar complaints about the same item can still support a claim. Talk to an attorney before assuming it is too late, and if any part of the product remains, stop using it and hold onto it.

items.question: What does LawProactive charge, and how does the attorney get paid?
items.answer: LawProactive is free to use and is not a law firm. We simply connect you with an independent attorney in our network who handles product liability cases in Contra Costa County. Those attorneys work on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery in your case.
